title: The translation program's accuracy-first commitment
statement: The corpus's own source-text translations (the -woh library editions) are produced under a published, checkable commitment: philological accuracy before the framework lens, with every lens-relevant divergence confined to the labelled commentary apparatus and never written into the translated text, glossary decisions recorded and adjudicated rather than improvised, and contested renderings escalated for review; the commitment is a rule the project binds itself to, and its observance is verifiable against the published apparatus.

includes: The rule: accuracy before lens — the translated text answers to the source language and scholarly defensibility; the framework's readings live in the commentary, labelled
The apparatus that makes it checkable: per-verse commentary for divergences, glossary records with claim-type rationales, editorial and review stages with escalation for speculative entries
The verification claim, which earns the direct label: whether a published -woh edition observes the rule is checkable by inspection of its text against its apparatus
excludes: Any claim that the translations are lens-free; the program's honesty is the labelled lens, not its absence
Quality claims about specific renderings; each book's apparatus carries its own record
The translation program's operational tooling, which is process, not commitment
External translations in the library, which the program does not govern

source_references.locator: The canon whose readings the lens carries — confined, under this rule, to the commentary layer of every -woh edition
The text-critical standard the accuracy side answers to

alternatives.statement: A lens confined to commentary still shapes the text through glossary choices and rendering defaults; the accuracy-first rule understates the frame's reach into the translation itself.
A project verifying its own rule-observance certifies itself; the commitment is checkable in principle but unchecked by anyone outside.

revision_triggers: The program's published rules change the commitment's content.
An external review documents lens-leakage into a published text, vindicating the leakage objection and requiring the edition's correction.
Corpus prose begins claiming lens-free translation, which this record excludes.
